verdict.rationale: Microsoft's setup docs describe scanning a QR code with the camera to add an account, with manual entry as the fallback. The app supports non-Microsoft accounts such as Amazon and Google and generates OATH one-time codes that work offline. Community reports of a QR-scan overwrite dialog are limited to accounts sharing the same username and are contradicted by other users, so this is an edge-case caveat, not a dispute of the core flow. Missing for 10: an explicit first-party step-by-step for adding a third-party TOTP account by QR and seeing codes immediately, and consistent hands-on corroboration free of the reported overwrite issue.

support.subject: As an everyday user, I can scan a QR code and immediately start generating TOTP codes for a new account

citations.quote: If you can't use your camera to scan a QR Code, click **I can't scan the bar code** on your PC and tap **Enter code manually** on your mobile.
non-Microsoft accounts, such as Amazon, Facebook, Instagram and Google
They can also use an OATH verification code in the Authenticator app and enter it in a sign-in interface.
The codes don't require you to be on the internet or connected to data, so you don't need phone service to sign in.
